messages:
anna: quick RFC follow-up — we hit two weird edge-cases in staging around API key scoping that I want to sync on. TL;DR: project-scoped keys being used by a cross-project CI job, and proxy tokens that leak enum-level perms. thoughts? :thinking:

mike: can you paste the exact flows? I want to see the token shape + which checks failed.

anna: sure — first one is a job in project-b that needs read-only access to a dataset in project-a. we minted a project-b key and tried to call the dataset list endpoint in project-a; request rejected by our enforcer. payload looked like:

```json
{
  "kid": "proj-b-key-1",
  "iss": "redwood-api",
  "sub": "svc:ci-runner:proj-b",
  "scope": "project:proj-b:read",
  "aud": "redwood-api",
  "exp": 1710000000
}
```

anna: the enforcer denied because scope didn't include project-a. but the app owner insists a CI job should be able to read across projects with a deploy-time consent flow.

sophie: hmm — that sounds like two policy options: 1) allow explicit cross-project delegation (minted by user or admin with audit log), or 2) mandate cross-project tokens are minted by the destination project (broker pattern). both have tradeoffs.

devon: +1 for broker. if project-a issues a short-lived "grant" token to proj-b after an admin approves, we avoid permanent broad-scoped API keys. also easier for revocation.

mike: broker implies an endpoint like `POST /v1/projects/:dest/delegations` which returns a token with `aud=project-a` and `scp=read:datasets`. admin in project-a approves via console / CLI. log entry created.

anna: example mint flow UX: user in proj-b clicks "request read on dataset X in proj-a" -> notifier to project-a admins -> one-click approve -> token appears in proj-b secrets store. ephemeral: 1h.

sophie: second edge-case: proxy tokens. we saw a service create a long-lived proxy key with wildcard `resource:*` so an internal gateway could act on behalf of many services. that bypasses least-privilege.

devon: we should forbid wildcard resource scopes on long-lived API keys. allow wildcard only on short-lived brokered tokens and only if admin sets `allow_wildcards=true` in project policy. default false.

anna: policy question: should our authn layer evaluate hierarchical allowance like org -> project -> resource? current check is exact-match on `scope` string. maybe add policy engine to accept templates: `org:org-x:project:*` but need audit + stricter grant flow.

mike: template support is fine but must populate `aud` and `origin` claims. also embed `granted_by` and `grant_id` for audit. e.g., token claims:

```json
{
  "sub": "svc:gateway",
  "aud": "project-a",
  "scp": "resource:list,resource:read",
  "grant_id": "G-12345",
  "granted_by": "alice",
  "exp": 1710003600
}
```

sophie: one more subtlety: service-to-service impersonation for scheduled jobs. we had a job that needs to call multiple projects; making it a global service account is tempting. instead recommend: the job uses a single orchestrator identity that mints per-target short-lived tokens (subject to per-target policies). orchestrator must be audited.

devon: operationally, implement a broker with these checks: 1) require explicit target project in request, 2) require admin approval or pre-allowed partner list, 3) generate token with `aud=target` and `origin=orchestrator`, 4) store grant with TTL and revocation flag.

anna: question for infra-bot: can we add an event hook in Console so admin approvals become first-class (UI + webhook -> audit)?

infra-bot: auto-response: created issue INFRA-3124 to add approval webhook and admin-grant audit timeline. ETA: 2 sprints.

mike: for RBAC model mapping: map `scope` -> permission set in the policy DB, not raw string checks. that'll make future changes less brittle. also add tests: a small eval harness that simulates cross-project requests and ensures no silent bypass.

sophie: addendum: CLI UX — add `--request-cross-project` flag that prints the audit flow and estimated time-to-approve to reduce noise. and default token TTL = 1h for brokered tokens, 30d for direct project keys.

anna: sounds like consensus. action items: 1) devon + mike to prototype broker endpoint + policy checks (INFRA-3125), 2) infra-bot issue INFRA-3124 for console webhook, 3) sophie to PR CLI flag and docs. I'll open a follow-up RFC update with the grant lifecycle and example JWTs. thanks all :thumbsup:
